To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sharing behavior of a subject is influenced by the following: 1) the subject’s age, 2) the subject’s gender, 3) the number of friends, 4) the subject’s mobility patterns, 5) the type of data to disclose.
the sharing behavior of individuals is influenced by their social interaction inferred from their mobile phone usage, by their demographic information and by their self-reported personality traits.

(i) social interaction inferred from mobile phone data is an important predictor for the willingness to share personal data, (ii) demographic characteristics are not relevant predictors, while (iii) self-reported individual traits are relevant predictors for sharing behavior, and (iv) the prediction accuracy of the model increases with the number of features.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a novel aspect of the privacy debate, i.e. the factors affecting the disclosure of personal data in the context of mobile phones, and it contributes to a better understanding of the privacy concerns of the users of mobile devices.
the understanding of factors affecting the disclosure of personal data.
the factors affecting personal information disclosure in the mobile domain, and provides a better understanding of how to improve privacy protection in this domain.

the disclosure of personal data is a complex process that is influenced by many factors and that the decision of disclosing data is not a simple one.
the disclosure of personal information is affected by a combination of individual traits and social interactions, which can be inferred from the data collected by mobile phones.

, while social interactions and individual traits can be used to predict sharing behavior, the most relevant factor is the type of the data to be disclosed, which is not affected by any of these variables.

the analysis of mobile phone data can be used to infer the propensity of a subject to share personal information.
the analysis of mobile phone data is a valuable tool for understanding the sharing behavior of users.
